lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Reginald, Kendra here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Kendra. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the walking went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Being around for my family is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: When I walk I sleep better, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're already doing things to make it easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I'll set an alarm on my phone. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walking. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you wants this, and part of you is just worn out.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I walk 20 minutes on 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 8 and not a 5?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If getting started gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Claims 'once you decide, you follow through' though participant reported walking only about 1 day this week; praise not grounded in participant's report.
Participant raised blood sugar concern ('I need to get my sugar down'); coach did not explore it and jumped to the mall question.
'Did you try the mall?' references an unexplained prior context and is closed, cutting off the participant's exploration.

score.summary: Kendra used frequent complex reflections and autonomy-supporting language that drew out change talk about grandchildren, sleep and energy, and she built a concrete 20-minute, 5-day goal with a barrier plan. Weaknesses include an unsupported affirmation at line 32, an abrupt closed question at line 37 that skipped the participant's blood sugar concern, and no end-of-call summary.
strengths: Line 14 and line 39: complex reflections that name ambivalence ('Part of you is already moving') and deepen change talk.
Line 34: emphasize autonomy ('Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan') supports participant choice.
Line 49: open question about a backup plan built a practical barrier plan.
coaching_tips: Line 32: avoid praising follow-through the participant hasn't shown; reflect what they actually said about walking days instead.
Line 36: when the participant names blood sugar, explore it ('What's your sugar concern about?') before moving on.
Line 37: replace the closed 'Did you try the mall?' with an open question that connects to what the participant just said.
Before closing, summarize the goal, confidence rating and backup plan in the participant's own words (line 51 came too soon).
